text:
Them 1: Hey, long time no see! How was the trip? Did you end up going to the coast?
You: We did, it rained the whole time but the kids loved it anyway.
Them 1: Ha, that is the way it goes. We were lucky, the sun came out on the Saturday.
You: Nice. And how are your two doing at school now?
Them 1: The little one just lost a tooth and has been telling everybody, the older one is obsessed with football.
You: Mine too, we spent most of the weekend kicking a ball around the garden.
Them 1: The garden is a disaster here, the lawn has gone completely brown after the heat.
You: Same. I keep saying I will water it and then I forget.
Them 1: You and me both. So what is new at the office, anything exciting happening?
You: Not much, we moved desks last month and the coffee machine is finally fixed.
Them 1: That is the real news right there.
You: Honestly it is. People were getting desperate.
Them 1: I can imagine. Oh, by the way, did you see the match on Sunday, that last goal was incredible.
You: I missed it, we were stuck in traffic coming back. Was it as good as everybody says?
Them 1: Better, my neighbour actually cried, he has supported them for forty years.
You: Wow. Maybe I should watch the highlights tonight.
Them 1: You should. Anyway, I wanted to ask whether you are coming to the barbecue next month?
You: Wouldn't miss it. Should I bring something? I can do a salad or the dessert.
Them 1: Dessert would be great, nobody ever brings dessert.
You: Done. I will make that lemon tart you liked last time.
Them 1: Perfect. Oh and somebody mentioned pricing on some software you were looking at, was that for work?
You: Ah, just a quick look at something, nothing decided, I will tell you when there is news.
Them 1: Fair enough. How is your mum, did she get the hip sorted?
You: She did, she is walking again and complaining about the physio, which means she is feeling better.
Them 1: Brilliant news, give her my love.
You: I will. How about your dad, is he still doing the marathon thing?
Them 1: He is, he did a half marathon in the spring and now he wants a full one, we cannot stop him.
You: Good for him. I get tired just thinking about it.
You: Are you still doing the Thursday football with the old crowd?
Them 1: When my knee allows it. I pulled something in the spring and I am being sensible, for once.
You: Sensible is not a word anyone would use about that group.
Them 1: True, last time somebody turned up in sandals. Sandals! He slipped in the first five minutes.
You: That is brilliant. Was he hurt?
Them 1: Only his pride. We have not let him forget it, there is a photo going around.
You: Send me the photo, I need it.
Them 1: I will. Oh, did you ever sort out the car, the one making the funny noise?
You: Yes, it was a loose bracket, forty minutes and a bill I would rather not discuss.
Them 1: That sounds about right. Ours needs new tyres before the winter, I keep putting it off.
You: Do it soon, my brother left it too late once and slid into a hedge.
Them 1: Good advice, I will book it for the weekend. Have you been watching anything good on television?
You: We finally started that detective series everyone raves about, three episodes in and I have no idea who did it.
Them 1: Do not tell me anything, I am about to start it myself.
You: My lips are sealed. It is slow at the beginning but worth it.
Them 1: Noted. Right, you must have a hundred things to do, so go.
Them 1: Me too. Right, I should let you go, I have to pick up the little one in ten minutes.
You: Of course. Lovely to catch up, let us not leave it so long next time.
Them 1: Agreed, see you at the barbecue!
You: See you there, take care.
